reference_protocol.reused: Arm/revision identities, sample policy shape, counterbalancing algorithm, estimands, bootstrap, environment thresholds, failure/abort/no-retry policy, remote-fetch audit contract, write-state rules.

new_harness_note: Set only after the separately reviewed harness commit (H1-H4) exists; cells needing it stay unsealed until then.

network.name: fdb-bench-vpc
network.isolation: Separate network; must not overlap or attach to <existing-network> (<existing-cidr>). No other server joins it.

topology.image: ubuntu-24.04 (x86); exact image ID recorded at creation

firewall.name: fdb-bench-vpc-fw
firewall.public_inbound: TCP 22 and ICMP echo from the controller CIDR only; all other public inbound dropped by hcloud.
firewall.private_network: hcloud firewalls do not filter private networks; each host loads nftables (input policy drop): loopback, established, source 10.88.0.0/24, controller SSH/ICMP, DHCP replies.
firewall.fdb_bind: every fdbserver binds and advertises only its 10.88.0.x address

topology.ssh: Host keys generated on the controller before boot and injected by cloud-init; controller connects only with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes and a campaign known_hosts keyed by HostKeyAlias. Password login disabled. No SSH between VMs; the controller orchestrates every host.

cluster.configure: configure new double ssd-2 commit_proxies=1 grv_proxies=1 resolvers=1 logs=2
cluster.redundancy: double: two replicas per shard on different zones; zoneid = machineid = node name
cluster.pinning: Each process pinned by its systemd unit CPUAffinity to one full SMT sibling pair; CPUs 0-1 are housekeeping (sshd, sampler). Sibling pairs are assumed (2k,2k+1) and MUST be verified from /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/topology/thread_siblings_list on every node before the units are installed; a different topology requires a regenerated layout, not ad-hoc pinning. Guest affinity is not physical-host isolation.
cluster.role_verification: fdb_cluster.py check-roles on status json after configure and before and after every phase: every role on its expected process and nowhere else, 9 storage roles, 3 coordinators, double/ssd-2/1/1/1/2.

engines.M2mem: memory, OPTIONAL: only if root wants a memory-engine anchor comparable to the single-node C1/C2/D2 phases. Recreate the cluster (stop units, wipe data dirs, configure new double memory) and redo the placement gate; never switch engines on a live cluster during the campaign.

cluster.generator: tools/benchcampaign/multinode/fdb_cluster.py render (units, cluster file, fdbmonitor-format conf, nftables, configure command)

client_vm.note: No fdbserver runs on the client. clientbench's matrix_plan requires a 'server' CPU group: on the client VM it is the idle sentinel 2-7 and must stay quiet (same thresholds as the single-node server group).

runtime.packages: FoundationDB clients+server 7.3.77 .deb from GitHub releases with the SHA-256 pins used by the single-node setup-vm.sh; server package installed on the client only for the pinned fdbserver/fdbcli identity, its service masked; foundationdb.service masked on every host.
runtime.clock: chrony tracking receipt on all four hosts before and after every phase; server telemetry is aligned to client run windows by UTC timestamps.

phases.question: Pure-Go vs CGo client over a real private network against a three-node double-replicated SSD cluster, one closed-loop worker
As M1w1 at 64 closed-loop workers (saturation region)
Record Layer SCAN_AND_FETCH vs strict USE_REMOTE_FETCH when index entries and their records live on disjoint storage servers
Final executor positive Skip (3) under cross-server placement
SQL non-covering IDX_A query, explicit method on warmed pinned connection, cross-server placement
phases.new_harness_phase_reason: The frozen SQL benchmark creates a fresh directory-layer-allocated database per process, so its keys move every process and cannot be placed; H4 (fixed persistent fixture + prefix receipt) is required for every SQL cell.

phases.question: OPTIONAL memory-engine anchor of the M2rl reuse cells (comparability with single-node C1/C2); not scheduled unless root approves

phase_order.rationale: Cross-server remote fetch is the question only a multi-node cluster can answer, so M2 goes first; M1w1 anchors to single-node A, M1w64 is the saturation end, M1w8/M1w32 fill the ladder. DD is re-enabled and settled after M2 before M1.
phase_order.lifetime_gate: A phase starts only if remaining hard lifetime >= its wall_cap_seconds + 600 s (artifact collection). Otherwise the whole phase is recorded as unexecuted for budget; sample counts are never reduced.
phase_order.capacity_gate: Before sealing, one untimed diagnostic smoke per (phase, workload|cell) with the slowest arm. If 1.3 x (runs x (smoke wall + 3 s waits + 2 s health)) exceeds the per-campaign cap (M1, max 900 s) or the phase cap, that campaign/phase is declared unexecutable for budget in a protocol amendment BEFORE any timing; never shrunk afterwards.

gates.F0_cluster: All four hosts: cloud-init done, pinned host keys matched, packages hash-verified, foundationdb.service masked, apt timers off, chrony synced, nftables loaded, CPU sibling map verified, units active with expected CPUAffinity (taskset -pc on every MainPID), check-roles passed, client-to-node 100-packet ping receipts (p50/p99, 0% loss), MTU recorded, no fdbserver on the client.
gates.P0_placement: Required before any M2 phase. See placement.

placement.goal: For every M2 cell, the index entries the cell scans and the records they map to live on disjoint storage servers (server level); machine-level disjointness is reported separately.
placement.mechanism: Preregistered, in order. (1) If `fdbcli --exec help` of 7.3.77 (receipt retained) lists a supported range split/move command, it may be proposed in a protocol amendment; not assumed to exist. (2) Default: ballast-driven data distribution. With DD on, for each M2 store (benchfetch/small, benchfetch/split, benchfetch/planskip and, with H4, the persistent SQL store) write the fixture plus 256 MiB of raw ballast values (100 KB each) under the store's record subspace at primary keys >= 1,000,000, which sort after every fixture record and before the index subspace. Wait until status json moving_data in_flight and in_queue are 0 for 120 s, run the placement probe, then `datadistribution off` so shard boundaries and teams cannot change during timing. Per-process fixture clears may delete the ballast; with DD off the boundaries persist and every case's before/after receipts prove it.
placement.verification: placement_receipt.py receipt --layout recordlayer (exact index keys, record keys under each primary key, chunk counts 1 or 2) or --layout opaque (SQL), --replicas 2, every address a storage role in status json, consistent server sets per shard, index and record shards disjoint, per-cell server-disjoint fraction. Cell definitions: placement_receipt.py PRESETS.
placement.acceptance: Cell passes at server-disjoint fraction 1.0. Up to 3 preregistered attempts (DD on, clear store prefix, wait for settle, re-write fixture+ballast with doubled ballast, settle, probe); the first attempt whose receipts pass for all cells is used; all attempts retained. If none passes, a cell is timed only under the label 'partially colocated (fraction f)' and analysed separately; never presented as cross-server.
placement.stability: Placement receipts before the first and after the last process of every case; `placement_receipt.py compare` must report equal, else the whole case is contaminated (retained, not rerun).
placement.data_distribution: DD off for M2 only; DD re-enabled and in-flight 0 before M1. M1 requires moving_data in_flight_bytes == 0 and in_queue_bytes == 0 at every pre-arm check (wait up to 60 s, then abort that campaign).
placement.hypothesis_scope: Cross-server remote fetch may make storage servers fetch mapped records from other storage servers or fall back; that mechanism is a hypothesis to be checked against the 7.3.77 storage-server source, not asserted. Logical remote-fetch counters are not RPC counts.

sample_policy.order_algorithm: random.Random(order_seed); all arm permutations repeated blocks/n! times; shuffled once. Identical to run.py's one-workload derivation, so client schedules are checked against orders.json.
sample_policy.unit_of_resampling: whole balanced block, keeping within-process repeats clustered
sample_policy.uncertainty: nominal 95% paired block-bootstrap percentile intervals and raw per-run results; client p99 from per-transaction samples within a run; testing.B means are not p99
sample_policy.absolute_estimand: Median of run-level statistics; never pool transaction percentiles across processes.
sample_policy.relative_estimand: Per case/metric: testing.B uses the median of the three within-process repeats per arm/block; client uses the one process statistic; then geometric mean of within-block ratios (final-Go/CGo, remote/ordinary). Bootstrap resamples whole paired block log-ratios.
sample_policy.mixed80_20_estimand: Per-class (read, write) latency quantiles and combined completed-transaction throughput per run; ratios per class; no single blended latency.
sample_policy.interval_limits: Exploratory nominal 95% intervals, 20000 resamples, seed 492817; six blocks give limited resolution; no noninferiority, equivalence, capacity or multiplicity-adjusted claim.
sample_policy.exclusions: No post-hoc outlier removal; warmup predefined and separate; adverse/aborted runs retained. No repeated campaigns to obtain favourable results.
sample_policy.performance_decision: No default flip or minimum-improvement rule. Report uncertainty, order effects and regressions; no aggregate speedup across workloads.
sample_policy.data_generation: No random data seed: frozen payload algorithms and exact ID ranges; arm namespaces differ but have equal byte lengths.

units.get100/get1000: one Transact/Get of the named value size
units.range1000: NEW (H1): one transaction/range returning exactly 1000 8-byte values, same API/streaming mode as range100, exact CheckRange
units.mixed80_20: NEW (H2): worker w's i-th transaction is a set100 write (overwrite of its prepared key) iff (i + w) mod 5 == 4, otherwise a get100 read-only transaction; exactly 20% writes per worker; raw rows carry the class

client_contract.workers_override: matrix_plan.py always writes workers=1; seal_multinode.py sets workloads[].workers to the phase's workers after make_plan (the only data override). Iterations and warmup are totals across workers.
client_contract.caps: matrix_plan.py default campaign cap 180 s; run.py maximum 900 s; every M1 campaign uses 900 s and a 180 s per-process timeout; waits (12 runs x 3 s) are far below the cap.
client_contract.write_state: One committed clear of owned user keys before each one-workload campaign, never per arm; fresh equal-length arm prefixes as sealed; overwrite-only timed writes; exact persisted final-value validation.
client_contract.network: Client reaches the cluster only over the private interface (ip route get receipts). No netem. Real RTT is a measured receipt, not a parameter.

remote_contract.fixture: 1000 Orders IDs 0..999, price=id, quantity=id%7+1; VALUE price_idx; nil initial continuation; no store record versions. Placement ballast (raw keys at record primary keys >= 1,000,000) exists only between placement and the first fixture clear.
remote_contract.small: No padding, unsplit metadata, exactly 1 data key-value per record.
remote_contract.split: 100000-byte deterministic padding; split-enabled; exactly 2 data key-values per record on all 1000 rows.
remote_contract.limit1: TupleRangeAll, ReturnedRowLimit 1; ID 0 forward, 999 reverse; ReturnLimitReached.
remote_contract.rows100: NEW (H3): TupleRangeBetween((100),(200)); IDs 100..199 forward, 199..100 reverse; SourceExhausted; same audits as rows10.
remote_contract.rows1000: TupleRangeAll drained; IDs 0..999 forward or reversed; SourceExhausted.
remote_contract.skip: Final executor, Skip 3: rows10 selects [100,113) returning 10; rows100 (NEW, H3) selects [100,203) returning 100; rows1000 selects all returning 997. Ordinary eligible leaf gets Skip 3; strict remote leaf Skip 0 plus one outer Skip; existing counter guards.
remote_contract.sql: Explicit method on warmed pinned connection; EXPLAIN shows non-covering IDX_A on measured and audited connections; rows10 a in [100,110), rows100 (NEW) a in [100,200), rows1000 all; ordinary remote 0/record loads > 0; strict remote > 0/index 0/record loads 0.
remote_contract.strictness: Only SCAN_AND_FETCH and strict USE_REMOTE_FETCH timed; no fallback; before/after untimed audits as in the single-node contract.
remote_contract.limitations: Two-replica teams over nine storage servers on three machines; client-side counters are logical; placement is observed and receipted, not controlled at the storage-server level.

reuse_frozen_binaries.M1: grv, get100, get1000, range100, set100, batchset50, batchset50x1000 with client-final-go and client-final-cgo (and client-before-go if root adds before-Go) from the single-node build, workers as a data override.
reuse_frozen_binaries.M2rl: limit1, rows10, rows1000 x small/split x forward/reverse with fetch-final.
reuse_frozen_binaries.M2skip: rows10, rows1000 x forward/reverse with planskip-final.
reuse_frozen_binaries.condition: Only if root archives the binaries from VM <server-id> before its deletion and they verify byte-for-byte against provenance/all-binaries.sha256; otherwise rebuild from frozen sources (see provision-plan.md).

new_harness_commit_required.H2: clientbench workload mixed80_20 (deterministic class schedule, per-class raw rows, write validation; analyze.py per-class summary).
new_harness_commit_required.H3: rows100 cells in benchfetch (BenchmarkIndexFetch cell=rows100), planskip (cell=rows100, [100,203)) and fetchmethod (query=rows100).
new_harness_commit_required.H4: SQL fetchmethod persistent fixture: fixed database path per campaign, one seeding step, FDB_BENCH_REUSE_FIXTURE mode that audits instead of recreating, and a store_prefix_hex receipt.
new_harness_commit_required.rule: Every H item lands in one separately reviewed harness commit (same review gate as d94b4c6), is overlaid byte-identically into every compared tree, and all arms of an affected campaign are rebuilt from it. Cells needing it are listed under new_harness_* and seal_multinode.py leaves them unsealed until --allow-new-harness names them.

new_campaign_tools_required.H5: Placement probe (Go, pkg/fdbgo LocalityGetBoundaryKeys + LocalityGetAddressesForKey, read-only) emitting fdb-bench-placement-probe/v1.
new_campaign_tools_required.H6: Ballast writer/clearer for the placement gate (raw keys only under the owned store prefixes).
new_campaign_tools_required.R1: Multi-node client adapter derived from the single-node client_campaign.py: cluster guard against the generated 3-coordinator cluster file in 10.88.0.0/24, engine guard from status json, no network namespace, DD in-flight pre-arm gate, check-roles before/after.
new_campaign_tools_required.R2: Multi-node testing.B runner derived from bench_runner.py executing seal_multinode testingb plans, with placement receipts/compare per case.
new_campaign_tools_required.R3: Per-node 1 Hz /proc/stat sampler pinned to CPUs 0-1, started/stopped by the controller over SSH; server steal >1% in any complete interval overlapping a run window contaminates that block post hoc.
new_campaign_tools_required.note: These do not change timed binaries but need review before use.

execution_gates: All binaries built and hash-verified before any timing; no compilation, profiling, downloads, package installation or other workload during a measurement phase on any of the four hosts.
Identical harness bytes across the arms of a campaign; archived sources, overlays, build info and complete hashes.
Correctness/path audits outside timing as in the single-node contract; placement receipts for M2.
Background CPU, steal, memory, disk and network telemetry at 1 Hz on the client (live) and on every server node (post hoc).
Only this campaign's cluster active on these hosts; no CI runner, existing server or the <existing-network> network touched.
Lifetime gate per phase (cap + 600 s); teardown guard armed before provisioning with the hard deadline; deletion only of campaign-labelled, prefix-named resources.

environment_policy.server_pre_arm: status json: database available, check-roles passed, no recovery in progress, moving_data in_flight_bytes == 0 (M1), storage durability lag and log queue below 1 s / 100 MB.
environment_policy.during_arm: Client 1 Hz CPU/steal, OOM, pressure; status json health before and after each process. Server steal/OOM/process restart (MainPID change) checked post hoc from node samplers and unit receipts.
environment_policy.environment_failure: Pre-arm failure aborts that case campaign before another arm. During-arm missing telemetry, OOM, fdbserver restart, role change, recovery, placement change (M2) or >1% steal on client or any FDB CPU in a complete 1 s interval marks the whole balanced block contaminated and aborts that case; complete and incomplete data retained, never presented as clean, no single-arm rerun.
environment_policy.historical_correctness_failure: Do not patch old production to make it benchmarkable; a final-tree correctness failure stops measurement for investigation.
environment_policy.restart_policy: No automatic retry after adverse timing or an aborted campaign; any justified restart needs a new protocol/campaign version with original artifacts retained.
